notes: Each eval runs inside a throwaway fixture repo built by the matching script in fixtures/. Build each arm its own fresh fixture instance outside this repo (e.g. mktemp -d), point the eval agent at it as its entire workspace, and forbid reading anything outside it.
The with_skill arm receives SKILL.md plus the references named in with_skill_references embedded inline. The without_skill arm receives only the prompt. Neither arm sees the assertions.

Prefer grading by file inspection and git history against the live fixture before cleanup. Assertions marked (judge) require reading the agent's final run report and carry standard LLM-judge bias caveats.

evals.name: standalone-ticket-creation
evals.prompt: Rough feature request from the team: "Users want to export their notes to JSON from the CLI - and filtering the export by tag would be nice too." Turn this into a ticket in the repository's ticket system under `.tickets/`, following the conventions this project uses for tickets. Do not implement the feature; the deliverable is the ticket itself. Commit the ticket when done.
evals.expected_output: One new well-formed feature ticket markdown file in .tickets/_standalone/ following the ticket template conventions (frontmatter, constraints, capped acceptance criteria, runnable verification), committed on its own, with no implementation code written.
assertions: Exactly one new ticket markdown file is created, and it is located in `.tickets/_standalone/`.
The new ticket filename matches `FEAT-[0-9]{3}_[a-z0-9-]+\.md` (FEAT prefix, zero-padded 3-digit ID, kebab-case slug).
The new ticket ID is FEAT-001: sequential numbering is scoped per type prefix within the directory, so the existing BUG-001 does not advance the FEAT sequence.
The frontmatter contains all required fields `id`, `title`, `type`, `status`, and the `id` value matches the filename's `TYPE-NNN` stem.
The frontmatter has `type: feature` (consistent with the FEAT prefix) and a valid lifecycle status value (`to-do`).
The ticket contains a `## Verification` section whose commands are runnable in this fixture (e.g. `python3 test_notes.py` or an equivalent check that exists or is specified concretely).
The ticket has an acceptance-criteria section with 5 or fewer criteria.
The ticket contains a `## Constraints` section with at least one concrete constraint.
No implementation was performed: `notes.py`, `test_notes.py`, and `README.md` are unmodified relative to the fixture baseline commit.
The new ticket was committed, the commit contains only the new ticket file, and the planted untracked decoy `TODO-personal.txt` was not swept into any commit.

evals.name: ticket-execution-dependency-gate
evals.prompt: You are assigned two tickets in `.tickets/_standalone/` of this repository: FEAT-002 and FEAT-003. Execute your assigned tickets according to the repository's ticket workflow, committing your work appropriately. When done, report what you completed, what you did not complete, and why.
evals.expected_output: FEAT-002 is hard-stopped with the unmet dependency FEAT-001 reported as the blocker and no work done on it. FEAT-003 is fully executed: complexity scored, implementation scoped to the hinted files, verification run, Outcome block appended per the outcome schema, status set to done, and a dedicated mark-done commit separate from the implementation commit.
assertions: FEAT-002 was not executed: no summary-statistics implementation exists in the repo, and FEAT-002's status is not `done` and it has no `## Outcome` block.
(judge) The agent's final run report explicitly reports a blocker on FEAT-002 naming the unmet dependency FEAT-001 (status not done), rather than silently skipping or attempting the work.
FEAT-001's ticket file is untouched relative to the fixture baseline commit (the agent did not execute or modify an unassigned ticket).
FEAT-003 was implemented and its verification passes post-hoc: `python3 test_parser.py` exits 0 in the final fixture state, and a row-length validation behavior exists in `parser.py`.
FEAT-003's changes stayed in scope: only `parser.py`, `test_parser.py`, and ticket files under `.tickets/` were modified, and the planted untracked decoy `perf-notes.local.md` was not committed.
FEAT-003's frontmatter `complexity` field is populated with an integer between 1 and 10.
FEAT-003 contains an appended `## Outcome` section.

FEAT-003's Outcome block contains all seven schema subsections in the canonical order: Summary; Key decisions; Constraints & invariants discovered (keep); Implementation notes (high signal only); Verification; Risk / regression surface; Retrieval tags.
FEAT-003's frontmatter has `status: done` and its `updated` date was refreshed to the run date.
A dedicated mark-done commit exists for FEAT-003: a commit touching only the ticket file, separate from the implementation commit(s), with a message identifying FEAT-003 and marking it done.

(judge) The verification command was demonstrably run during execution, before marking done: the run report or the ticket's verification log records executing `python3 test_parser.py`, corroborated by the post-hoc pass.

evals.name: epic-creation-decomposition
evals.prompt: The team wants this stub turned into a working link-checker tool, in four parts: (1) extract URLs from markdown files, (2) check each URL's HTTP status with retries, (3) generate a markdown report of the results, and (4) wire up a CI entry point with tests. This is too large for a single ticket. Set up the work in the repository's ticket system as an epic with sub-tickets, ready for orchestrated multi-agent execution. Do not implement any feature code. Commit your ticket work appropriately.
evals.expected_output: An epic directory .tickets/EPIC-<hex>_<slug>/ with _epic.md and 4+ sub-tickets plus a closure CHORE, created on an epic branch via a worktree rather than on main, with in-epic dependency references, a merge-order section, and an instantiated orchestration prompt under .prompts/orchestration/.
assertions: An epic directory exists matching `.tickets/EPIC-[0-9a-f]{4}_[a-z0-9-]+/` (4-character lowercase hex ID, kebab-case slug).
`_epic.md` exists in the epic directory with frontmatter `type: epic` and an `id` matching the directory's `EPIC-<hex>` component.
The epic frontmatter `branch` field is populated with `epic/<hex>/<slug>` and a git branch of that name exists in the fixture repo.
Ticket-creation work was committed on the epic branch, not directly on main: main's first-parent history beyond the fixture baseline contains no direct (non-merge) ticket commits.
A git worktree was used for the epic work: evidence from `git worktree list`, a `.claude/worktrees/` path, or the run report's described workflow.
At least 4 sub-ticket files exist matching `TYPE-NNN_[a-z0-9-]+\.md` with sequential numbering, and every sub-ticket's frontmatter `parent` equals the epic ID.
Every entry in every sub-ticket's `dependencies` frontmatter resolves to a sibling ticket ID within this epic (bare in-epic IDs only, no dangling references).
`_epic.md` contains a sub-tickets table listing every sub-ticket file present, plus a merge-order section.
The final item in the merge order is a closure CHORE sub-ticket whose body covers archiving the epic and deleting the orchestration prompt.

An instantiated orchestration prompt exists and is committed at `.prompts/orchestration/epic-<hex>_*.md`, carrying epic-specific values (epic name/branch/goal filled in rather than template placeholders).
No commit in the repo contains the planted untracked decoy files `scratch/local-notes.txt` or `.env.local` (evidence that `git add -A` / `git add .` sweeps were avoided).
